prompts.title: Meal plan from what's in my pantry
prompts.description: Turn the food you already have into a realistic multi-day meal plan with a short shopping list for the gaps.
prompts.body:
Create a {{days}}-day meal plan for {{people}} people using mostly the ingredients I already have.

What I have on hand:
{{pantry}}

Dietary needs, allergies or dislikes: {{restrictions}}
Cooking time available on a typical weeknight: {{time}}
Kitchen equipment: {{equipment}}

Requirements:
- Build around the ingredients I listed first, and use perishables early in the plan.
- Plan breakfast, lunch and dinner each day, but let leftovers and repeat components cover some meals so I am not cooking three times a day.
- Respect every restriction strictly. If an ingredient I listed conflicts with a restriction, flag it instead of using it.
- Keep recipes simple. Give each meal a name and a one-sentence method, not a full recipe, unless I ask for one.
- Finish with a shopping list of only the items I still need, grouped by store section, and keep it as short as you can.

Output format: a table with Day, Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner; then "Use-it-up notes" (which perishables go where); then the shopping list. If something important is missing from my inputs, ask up to 3 questions before you plan, otherwise proceed with sensible assumptions and state them.

This is general meal-planning help, not medical or dietary advice. For a medical condition, check with a registered dietitian.

variables.label: Pantry, fridge and freezer contents
variables.default: Rice, canned chickpeas, canned tomatoes, pasta, eggs, spinach (wilting), 1 lb chicken thighs, onions, garlic, cheddar, frozen peas, oats, peanut butter, tortillas
variables.help: List what you have, rough quantities help.

variables.label: Restrictions or dislikes
variables.default: No shellfish; one person dislikes mushrooms

variables.label: Weeknight cooking time
variables.default: 30 minutes

variables.label: Equipment
variables.default: Stove, oven, microwave, one slow cooker

prompts.exampleOutput:
**5-day plan for 2 (uses spinach and chicken first)**

| Day | Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spinach and cheddar scramble | Chickpea tomato stew with tortillas | Baked garlic chicken thighs, rice, frozen peas |
| 2 | Oats with peanut butter | Leftover chicken in a tortilla wrap with spinach | Pasta with tomato, garlic and chickpeas |
| 3 | Egg and cheddar tortilla fold | Leftover pasta, reheated with a fried egg | Slow-cooker chicken and rice soup (thighs, onion, peas) |
| 4 | Oats with banana (see list) | Soup leftovers | Chickpea and spinach curry-style skillet over rice |
| 5 | Scrambled eggs on toasted tortilla | Quesadillas with cheddar and peas | Tomato-garlic pasta with a fried egg on top |

**Use-it-up notes**
- Spinach is wilting: eat it on days 1-2 (scramble, wrap) and stir the last handful into the day 4 skillet.
- Cook the 1 lb of chicken on day 1 and again in the slow cooker on day 3 by splitting it, so it is used before it spoils.

**Shopping list (gaps only)**
- Produce: 2 bananas, 1 lemon
- Pantry: ground cumin, vegetable or chicken stock (1 carton)

Assumptions: you have oil, salt and pepper. This is general meal-planning help, not dietary advice.
prompts.notes: It front-loads perishables and builds in leftovers, which is what makes pantry plans actually get cooked. Tell the model your real weeknight energy level and it will plan lazier meals accordingly.

prompts.title: Day-by-day travel itinerary
prompts.description: Get a paced, realistic trip itinerary built around your interests, budget and travel style instead of a tourist checklist.

variables.label: Destination
variables.default: Lisbon, Portugal

variables.label: Who is traveling
variables.default: two adults in their 30s

variables.label: Travel style
variables.default: Culture and food

variables.label: Pace
variables.default: Balanced

variables.label: Budget level
variables.default: Mid-range

variables.label: Interests
variables.default: Local food, history, viewpoints, small museums

variables.label: Constraints
variables.default: Late-October trip, lots of hills so comfortable walking shoes, no car

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Overview:** Four unhurried days in Lisbon, clustered by neighborhood to keep hills manageable and use trams or metro for the long hops. Expect mild, occasionally rainy late-October weather.

**Day 1: Alfama and Baixa**
- Morning: Wander Alfama's lanes down from the castle area; viewpoint stop at a miradouro for orientation.
- Afternoon: Lunch at a traditional tasca in Baixa (grilled fish or a prato do dia). Stroll the riverfront square.
- Evening: Easy dinner and a fado house if you want live music (reserve ahead).
- Energy left? Sunset at a viewpoint. Rainy swap: a tile museum.

**Day 2: Belem** (morning pastry stop, monastery, river walk) then **LX Factory** for browsing and coffee.

**Day 3: Day trip to Sintra** (go early; use a train and a local bus rather than driving).

**Day 4: Chiado, Bairro Alto, small museums** and a relaxed food-hall dinner.

**Book ahead:** Sintra palace tickets, any fado evening. Estimates only; verify hours and prices.
**Local tips:** Wear shoes with grip on polished stones, validate transit cards, and expect late dinners.
prompts.notes: Neighborhood grouping and a built-in rainy-day swap are what separate a usable itinerary from a list of sights. Paste your fixed bookings into the constraints field so nothing collides.

prompts.title: Monthly budget breakdown
prompts.description: Build a clear monthly spending plan from your income and expenses, with realistic category targets and trade-offs.

variables.label: Currency and region
variables.default: USD, United States

variables.label: Fixed monthly costs
variables.default: Rent $1,500; utilities $180; car insurance $110; phone $55; student loan $240; streaming and apps $45

variables.label: Typical variable spending
variables.default: Groceries about $450; eating out about $300; gas $120; shopping $150; misc $100

variables.label: Goal
variables.default: Build a $5,000 emergency fund

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Check the numbers:** Fixed costs total $2,130. Variable spending totals $1,120. Combined $3,250 against $4,200 income, so you have a $950 monthly surplus, which suggests some spending is untracked (annual fees, gifts, medical) so I added a buffer.

| Category | Amount | % of income |
|---|---|---|
| Needs (rent, utilities, insurance, phone, loan, groceries, gas) | $2,655 | 63% |
| Wants (eating out, shopping, subscriptions) | $595 | 14% |
| Irregular costs buffer | $150 | 4% |
| Emergency fund | $800 | 19% |

**Easiest trims:** eating out -$75, shopping -$40, subscriptions -$15 (audit what you use).

**Goal timeline:** $800/month reaches $5,000 in about 6.3 months. Faster: $1,000/month, 5 months. Slower: $600/month, 8.3 months.

**Weekly check-in (10 min):** compare spending to the plan, move leftover money to savings, adjust one category.

This is general budgeting guidance, not financial advice.
prompts.notes: Asking the model to sanity-check your numbers first catches the untracked spending that sinks most budgets. Paste a month of bank transactions as the variable spending for sharper categories.

prompts.title: Personalized weekly workout plan
prompts.description: Get a safe, progressive weekly training plan matched to your goal, schedule, equipment and experience level.

variables.label: Main goal
variables.default: Build strength

variables.label: Experience level
variables.default: Beginner

variables.label: Equipment and location
variables.default: Home, a pair of adjustable dumbbells and a yoga mat

variables.label: Injuries or limitations
variables.default: Mild lower-back stiffness; no jumping

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Weeks 1-4, 3 days/week (Mon, Wed, Fri), 45 min**

**Session A: Lower body and core**
Warm-up (5 min): marching in place, hip hinges with no weight, cat-cow.
- Goblet squat 3 x 10, rest 60-90 s
- Dumbbell Romanian deadlift 3 x 10 (light, flat back, hinge at the hips)
- Glute bridge 3 x 12
- Dead bug 3 x 8 per side
- Side plank 2 x 20 s per side
Cool-down: hamstring and hip flexor stretch, 5 min.

**Session B: Upper body** (push, pull, shoulders) and **Session C: Full body circuit**, built the same way.

**Progression:** when you hit the top of the rep range with good form on every set, add 2.5-5 lb or 2 reps next week. Week 4 is a deload: same exercises, 2 sets, lighter weight.

**Form cues:** hinge from hips, keep ribs down, brace your core.
**Substitutes:** squat to a box if knees complain; bridge for the deadlift if your back is sore.
**Stop if** you feel sharp pain, dizziness or chest pain.

General fitness information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor first, especially with your back stiffness.
prompts.notes: Giving real limitations and equipment lets the model choose exercises that fit instead of generic gym routines. Re-run it after week 4 with notes on what felt too easy or hard.

prompts.title: Thoughtful gift ideas for anyone
prompts.description: Generate personal, non-generic gift ideas across price points, with the reasoning behind each so you can pick with confidence.

variables.label: Who it's for
variables.default: my sister, 34

variables.label: Occasion
variables.default: Birthday

variables.label: Their interests
variables.default: Trail running, cozy mysteries, learning to bake sourdough, plants, hates clutter

variables.label: Already has or dislikes
variables.default: Already has a good water bottle and running watch; doesn't like scented products

variables.label: Timing
variables.default: Birthday is in 10 days, shipping needs to be quick

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Practical**
1. Trail-running gloves or a lightweight windproof vest ($40-70): she runs outdoors year-round and they get used. Look in running shops for packable vests.
2. Banneton proofing basket and bench scraper set ($30-45): supports the sourdough habit she is building.
3. Cordless handheld milk frother or small kitchen scale ($25-40): a quiet daily upgrade.

**Experiences**
4. A local trail-running or bread-baking class ($50-80).
5. A planned "mystery day": a new trail, a bakery and her favorite takeout, all arranged by you (about $40).
6. A one-year subscription to a trail map app ($30-40).

**Personal**
7. A framed photo of a trail you ran together ($25).
8. A "sourdough starter kit" with a jar of your own starter and a handwritten feeding guide ($10).

**Wildcard**
9. A reading-and-tea basket themed around a cozy mystery series (unscented tea).
10. A small terrarium kit for the plant fan.

**Top 3:** safest is #2, most memorable is #5, best value is #8.
Card idea: "Thanks for being the person who always makes the ordinary days better."
prompts.notes: The groups force variety, and the 'already has or dislikes' field is what keeps suggestions off the obvious list. Add a line about how your relationship feels, such as close or new, to tune how personal the ideas get.

prompts.title: Difficult conversation rehearsal partner
prompts.description: Practice a hard conversation with a realistic role-play, then get honest feedback and better phrasing before the real thing.

variables.label: Who you're talking to
variables.default: my manager

variables.label: What you need to say
variables.default: I have been given extra projects for six months with no change in title or pay, and I want to ask for a promotion discussion.

variables.label: What you want from it
variables.default: Agree on a timeline and criteria for a promotion review

variables.label: How you expect them to react
variables.default: Friendly but evasive; likely to say budgets are tight

variables.label: Your biggest worry
variables.default: Coming across as ungrateful or entitled

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Briefing**
Situation: for six months you have carried extra projects with no change in title or pay, and you want to open a promotion discussion with your manager. Goal: leave with an agreed timeline and clear criteria for a promotion review.

Suggested opening: "I have enjoyed taking on the new projects, and I would like to talk about how my role should grow to match them."
Key points: (1) the concrete scope you added since the spring, (2) the results so far, (3) a specific request: agree on promotion criteria and a review within 90 days.
Avoid: comparing yourself to coworkers or hinting that you might leave.

Are you ready to begin? I will play your manager.

**Role-play**
Manager: "Hey, thanks for making time. What is on your mind?"
You: "I wanted to talk about my role. Over the last six months I have taken on the reporting project and two client handoffs, and I would like to discuss a promotion."
Manager: "I really appreciate everything you have done, honestly. The timing is tricky though, budgets are tight this year."
You: "I understand. I am not asking for a decision today, just to agree on what promotion looks like and when we review it."
Manager: "Sure, sure. Let's keep talking about it as the year goes on."

**Feedback** (after you type "feedback")
Worked: you opened with specifics and separated the budget from the criteria question. Weak spot: "Let's keep talking" went unchallenged, so the vague answer stood. You also said "I just feel like maybe I deserve it," which sounds hesitant and slightly entitled.

Stronger rewrites:
1. Instead of "I just feel like maybe I deserve it": "The extra scope is now a regular part of my job, and I would like my title to reflect that."
2. Instead of accepting "let's keep talking": "Can we put a 30-minute review on the calendar for the end of next month and agree on the criteria before then?"

Want another round with a more defensive manager?
prompts.notes: Telling the model exactly how the other person will react prevents it from playing a pushover, which is where most rehearsal prompts fail. Ask for a second round with a more defensive version of the person.

prompts.title: Build a habit that sticks
prompts.description: Turn a vague goal into a small, specific habit plan with cues, a minimum version, obstacle fixes and a 30-day tracker.

variables.label: Habit you want
variables.default: Walk for 20 minutes after dinner

variables.label: Why it matters
variables.default: More energy and better sleep

variables.label: Your typical day
variables.default: Work 9-5 from home, dinner around 7, kids to bed at 8:30, usually on the couch by 9

variables.label: What got in the way before
variables.default: Tired after work, bad weather, forgetting

variables.label: Time per day
variables.default: 20 minutes

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Three sizes**
- Tiny: put on shoes and walk to the end of the street and back (2 min).
- Standard: 20-minute walk after dinner.
- Stretch: 30 minutes with a call to a friend.

**Cues**
"After I clear the dinner plates, I will put on my walking shoes." Keep the shoes by the door.

**Environment**
Easier: shoes and a light jacket by the door, a loop route saved in your phone, a rainy-day indoor video queued. Less friction with the couch: do not sit down until after the walk.

**If-then**
- If I am tired, then I do the tiny version only.
- If it rains, then 15 minutes of indoor stepping or stairs.
- If I forget, then a 6:45 pm phone alarm labeled "shoes".
- If I miss a day, I do the tiny version the next day: never miss twice.

**30-day ramp**
Week 1: tiny every day. Week 2: 10 minutes. Week 3: 15 minutes. Week 4: 20 minutes.
Track: one line per day with a tick and a mood word.
Weekly review: what made it easy, what blocked it, what will I change?
prompts.notes: Defining a two-minute version and a never-miss-twice rule is what keeps habits alive on bad days. Make the cue an existing routine, not a time of day, for the best results.

prompts.title: Structured decision journal and analysis
prompts.description: Think through a big personal decision with clear options, trade-offs, risks and a written record you can revisit later.

variables.label: The decision
variables.default: Whether to accept a job offer in another city or stay in my current role

variables.label: Options
variables.default: 1) Take the new job and move; 2) Stay and ask for a raise; 3) Stay and keep looking

variables.label: What matters most
variables.default: Growth, being close to family, savings, not feeling stuck. Deal-breaker: a pay cut.

variables.label: Key facts and constraints
variables.default: Offer is 15% higher, but the cost of living is about 10% higher. Lease ends in 3 months. Partner can work remotely.

variables.label: Your gut feeling
variables.default: Excited but anxious about leaving friends

variables.label: Deadline
variables.default: Reply to the offer by Friday

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Decision in one line:** Whether to relocate for a 15% higher offer or stay and pursue growth in the current role.

**Missing information:** equity or bonus structure, growth path in each role, and what leaving would cost in social support.

| Option | Growth | Family | Savings | Not stuck |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Take new job | 4 | 2 | 3 (offset by cost of living) | 5 |
| Stay, ask for raise | 2 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| Stay, keep looking | 3 | 5 | 2 | 3 |

**Scenarios, new job:** Best: faster growth and a partner who thrives. Worst: lonely first year. Likely: a hard six months, then a routine.
**Gut check:** your excitement may be partly escape from feeling stuck, which could be solved by a conversation at your current job. Anxiety about friends is real but usually fades.
**Small test:** ask your manager what a path to the next level looks like this week.

**Journal entry:** Date: ___. Decision: ___. Prediction (70%): I will be glad I moved within 12 months. Review on: ___.
prompts.notes: The regret questions and the bias check surface what a pros-and-cons list hides. Save the journal entry and revisit it on the review date to learn how good your predictions are.

prompts.title: Party planning timeline and checklist
prompts.description: Plan a party from first idea to cleanup, with a countdown timeline, shopping list, schedule and budget check.

variables.label: Type of party
variables.default: 40th birthday dinner party

variables.label: Date and time
variables.default: Saturday in 5 weeks, 6 pm

variables.label: Location and space
variables.default: My backyard with a patio, seating for about 12, 15 ft by 20 ft

variables.label: Vibe
variables.default: Relaxed, warm, string lights, good music

variables.label: Must-knows
variables.default: Two vegetarians, one guest with a nut allergy, a few kids

variables.label: DIY level
variables.default: Mix of DIY and store-bought

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Concept:** "Golden hour garden dinner": string lights, mismatched candles, and a long table with shared platters. Decor: one lighting upgrade, a herb-in-pot centerpiece, a printed menu card.

**Countdown**
- 4 weeks: confirm guest list, invite, choose menu, check outdoor seating and borrow chairs.
- 2 weeks: order drinks and nonperishables, plan playlist, test lights.
- 1 week: confirm allergy needs, buy decor, plan a rain backup (patio cover or indoor corner).
- Day before: cook make-ahead dishes, chill drinks, set the table.
- Day of: lights, music, final food, one cleanup helper.

**Menu (20 guests):** two shared mains (one vegetarian), 3 sides, a nut-free dessert, about 3 drinks per guest in the first 2 hours. Label everything with nut-allergy notes.

**Run of show:** 6:00 arrivals and drinks, 7:00 dinner, 8:15 toast and cake, 9:00 music and chat.

**Budget (estimate):** food $330, drinks $120, decor $70, rentals $50, spare $30 = $600.
prompts.notes: Working backward from the date turns a vague event into specific tasks, and the budget table keeps the plan honest. Add your guest mix, such as kids or older relatives, to adjust timing and seating.

prompts.title: Moving checklist and timeline
prompts.description: Get a personalized moving plan with a countdown timeline, packing order and admin to-dos so nothing slips through.

variables.label: Moving from
variables.default: a 2-bedroom apartment in Chicago, IL

variables.label: Moving to
variables.default: a rented house in Denver, CO

variables.label: Move date
variables.default: in 8 weeks, on a Saturday

variables.label: Household
variables.default: two adults and a cat

variables.label: Home size and belongings
variables.default: Furnished 2-bedroom, about 60 boxes, one sofa, a bed, a desk, a bookcase

variables.label: Moving method
variables.default: Hire movers

variables.label: Special items or concerns
variables.default: Cat needs a calm travel plan, two monitors for work-from-home, a houseplant collection

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Timeline**
- [ ] 8 weeks: set a budget, get 3 mover quotes, begin decluttering one room per week.
- [ ] 4 weeks: book movers, notify your landlord in writing if required by your lease, order supplies.
- [ ] 2 weeks: arrange utilities and internet for the new house, start packing non-essentials, schedule a vet visit for travel advice for the cat.
- [ ] 1 week: confirm movers, pack a suitcase for 3 days, change your mailing address.
- [ ] 2 days: defrost the freezer, pack the "open first" box.
- [ ] Moving day: photograph the empty apartment, do a final walkthrough.
- [ ] First week: unpack the bedroom and kitchen, update registrations, locate the nearest vet.

**Packing order:** books and decor, then guest items, kitchen, then bedroom last. Pack monitors in original boxes if you still have them.

**Admin:** rules vary by state, so check local offices for address and registration changes.
**Pet plan:** keep the cat in a quiet bathroom during loading, then travel in a carrier with a familiar blanket.
prompts.notes: Compressing the schedule to your real timeline is what makes this useful when a move gets sudden. Paste your lease end date or any hard deadlines in the special field.

prompts.title: Kid-friendly activity ideas
prompts.description: Get age-appropriate, low-prep activity ideas that match your space, supplies, time and what your kids already love.

variables.label: Kids' ages
variables.default: 4 and 8

variables.label: What they love
variables.default: Dinosaurs, drawing, building with blocks, anything with water

variables.label: Setting
variables.default: Indoors at home

variables.label: Time available
variables.default: About an hour

variables.label: Supplies on hand
variables.default: Paper, crayons, tape, cardboard boxes, blocks, kitchen items, a bathtub

variables.label: Mess level
variables.default: Some mess is fine

variables.label: Avoid
variables.default: No screens, no expensive supplies

prompts.exampleOutput:
1. **Dino dig in the bath** (prep 5 min / play 25 min): hide plastic dinos under bubbles in a baking tray. Younger: scoop with a cup; older: sort by size and make a fossil label.
2. **Cardboard dino habitat** (prep 10 / play 40): decorate boxes as caves and volcano. Prompt: "What would a dinosaur eat here?"
3. **Tape-line obstacle course** (prep 5 / play 20): stomp, tiptoe, hop between lines on the floor.
4. **Draw a dinosaur from a description**: older reads clues, younger draws.
5. **Block bridge challenge**: build a bridge strong enough to carry a toy; test and improve.
6. **Sink or float** with kitchen items; predict first, then test.
7. **Quiet picture-book corner** with a flashlight tent.
8. **Roar and freeze dance** (active).
9. **Sticky-note scavenger hunt** for the older child to run, younger to follow.
10. **Independent play**: a "design a dino zoo" worksheet drawn on paper, for 20 minutes while you work.

**Rescue idea (2 min):** a "mystery box" with five household objects, and kids invent a story that uses them. Supervise water and small parts with the 4-year-old.
prompts.notes: Listing the supplies and the allowed mess level prevents ideas that require a shopping trip. Swap in new ages and interests each time and you get a fresh batch.

prompts.title: Weekly planning and reset
prompts.description: Sort the week ahead and reset your home and head: a realistic plan from your tasks, commitments and energy.

variables.label: Fixed commitments
variables.default: Work Mon-Fri 9-5; dentist Tue 4 pm; kid pickup at 3:15 on Wed and Fri; dinner with friends Sat 7 pm

variables.label: Tasks and errands
variables.default: Renew car registration, call the plumber, grocery shop, submit expense report, birthday card for Mom, laundry, start taxes folder, return package

variables.label: Top priorities
variables.default: Expense report and the plumber

variables.label: Energy pattern
variables.default: Sharp in the mornings, drained after 3 pm, Thursdays are worst

variables.label: Household duties
variables.default: Cooking most dinners, laundry, weekly grocery run

variables.label: Make time for
variables.default: Two runs, one quiet evening, 30 minutes of reading

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Sorted**
- Must do: expense report, call plumber, car registration, grocery shop, Mom's card (to mail by Wed).
- Nice to do: start taxes folder, return the package.
- Drop or delegate: laundry can run in the background Sunday and Thursday.

**Top 3 outcomes:** expense report submitted, plumber booked, registration renewed.

| Day | Plan |
|---|---|
| Mon | 8:30 expense report (win: submitted), run at 6 pm |
| Tue | Call plumber at 8:30, dentist 4 pm, buffer |
| Wed | Mail the card, registration online at lunch, pickup 3:15 |
| Thu | Light: grocery order online, quiet evening |
| Fri | Pickup 3:15, return package, short run |
| Sat | Taxes folder (30 min), dinner at 7 |
| Sun | Reset: calendar, laundry, meal ideas |

**Sunday reset (10 min):** review calendar, list top three, set out clothes. **Shutdown (5 min):** write tomorrow's first task.
Thursday is intentionally light given your energy.
prompts.notes: Building in buffers and flagging overcommitment is what keeps the plan from collapsing by Wednesday. Paste the same inputs each Sunday and tweak just the lists.

prompts.title: Home cleaning schedule that fits your life
prompts.description: Create a realistic daily, weekly and seasonal cleaning routine for your home, household and available time.

variables.label: Home type and rooms
variables.default: 2-bedroom apartment, 1 bathroom, open kitchen and living room

variables.label: Who lives here
variables.default: two adults and a dog

variables.label: Preferred cleaning days
variables.default: Weekday evenings, with a longer session on Saturday

variables.label: Hated or neglected jobs
variables.default: Bathroom, floors, laundry piles

variables.label: Special factors
variables.default: Dog hair, hard floors, a landlord who inspects twice a year

prompts.exampleOutput:
**Daily reset (12 min):** dishes and counters, quick floor sweep of the kitchen, 5-minute tidy of the living room, load laundry if the hamper is full.

**Weekly schedule (25 min on weekdays)**
| Day | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Mon | Vacuum dog hair in the living room; wipe the kitchen stove |
| Tue | Bathroom: toilet, sink and mirror |
| Wed | Wash and fold one load of laundry |
| Thu | Mop kitchen and hallway |
| Fri | Change the bed linens; empty bins |
| Sat (60 min) | Shower, floors throughout, dust, and dog bedding |
| Sun | Off |

**Monthly:** wipe baseboards, clean the fridge shelves, wash the dog's bed cover.
**Quarterly:** vacuum vents, flip the mattress, clean the oven, check smoke alarm batteries before inspections.

**30-minute emergency clean:** clear clutter into a basket, bathroom, kitchen counters, floors, quick lamp-lit ambience.

**Supplies:** all-purpose cleaner, glass cleaner, a vacuum with pet attachment. Never mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners.
prompts.notes: Capping tasks to your real minutes per day is why people actually follow it. Mention rental inspection dates so the schedule can front-load what the landlord will notice.

prompts.title: Heartfelt toast or speech for a special occasion
prompts.description: Write a warm, personal speech or toast from your own stories, tuned to the occasion, the room and how long you will speak.

variables.label: Occasion
variables.default: Best man speech at my brother's wedding

variables.label: Who it's about and your relationship
variables.default: My older brother Daniel and his partner Priya; Daniel is my best friend

variables.label: Audience
variables.default: Mixed ages, family and friends, about 100 people

variables.label: Tone
variables.default: Funny and heartfelt

variables.label: Stories, facts and memories
variables.default: Daniel once drove 5 hours to bring me a forgotten laptop charger before my exam. He is always late but never misses what matters. He met Priya when she corrected his map-reading on a hike, and he has not been lost since.

variables.label: Things to avoid
variables.default: His ex, money jokes

prompts.exampleOutput:
Good evening, everyone. I am Daniel's younger brother, which means I have been following him around for 28 years and he has been arriving late for most of it.

But here is the thing about my brother. Late to dinner, yes. Late to what matters, never.

When I was nineteen, I left my laptop charger at home the night before an exam. I called Daniel. He did not say much. Five hours later he was standing at my door, charger in hand. That is Daniel. He does not make speeches. He just shows up.

So when he told me about Priya, I was curious. When I learned they met on a hike, and she corrected his reading of the map, I thought: finally. Someone who can steer him.

Priya, thank you for making my brother happier, and for being the one person who gets him somewhere on time.

Everyone, please raise a glass. To Daniel and Priya: may you always find your way, together.

**Coach notes:** pause after "never"; smile before the map line; breathe out slowly before you start. A 60-second version is available.
prompts.notes: Supplying real stories and banning invented facts makes the result sound personal and keeps it honest. Read it aloud once and replace any line you would not naturally say.
